name: Retrieval-grounded drafting
summary: Single model call grounded in retrieved documents. Human reviews and edits the draft before it is used.
when: Output is text a human will review. Latency tolerant. No actions taken on systems.
fails_when: Retrieval quality is poor or source documents are stale or contradictory.

name: Orchestrated multi-step with tool use
summary: One agent loop that calls typed tools against real systems, then produces a structured output.
when: The task needs live data from more than one system and the steps vary by input.
fails_when: Tools are unreliable or slow, or the model cannot tell when it is done.

name: Classify then route
summary: Cheap model classifies the input, then routes to a specialised prompt or a human queue.
when: High volume, mixed input quality, and a long tail that should go to humans.
fails_when: Categories overlap, or the long tail is bigger than anyone admitted.

name: Multi-agent with a supervisor
summary: A supervisor agent decomposes work to specialist sub-agents and reconciles their output.
when: Genuinely separable subtasks with different tools or knowledge, and long horizons.
fails_when: Subtasks are not actually independent. Usually premature. Try orchestrated single-agent first.

name: Human-in-the-loop approval gate
summary: Agent prepares an action and stops. A human approves before anything is written back.
when: The action is consequential, regulated, or hard to reverse.
fails_when: Approval volume overwhelms the humans, so they rubber-stamp and the gate becomes theatre.

name: Batch enrichment
summary: Offline pass over a backlog of records, writing structured fields back to a system of record.
when: Volume is high, latency does not matter, and output is structured rather than prose.
fails_when: Error rate is invisible because nobody sampled the output before trusting it.
